mechanism_narrative: A rise in GDP indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of GDP growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate increases borrowing and spending, stimulating economic growth and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of payroll employment growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of industrial production growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts indicates decreased demand for housing, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during periods of decreased housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate and a decrease in GDP indicate a monetary tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment rate indicates a weak labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower during periods of high unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales and a decrease in housing starts indicate a shift in consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of increased retail sales and decreased housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).
